# Experimental alpha contracts

The original provisional contracts use schema version `1.0`; the package/API version is
`0.1.0a1`/`1.0`. Implemented contracts do not establish supported live execution;
see [qualification](qualification.md).

## Ollama fixture contracts v2.4

The additive `driver-config`, `task-spec`, `worker-packet` and `packet-projection`
resources use version 2.4 with `claude-ollama-fixture/1`. Explicit
`OllamaDriverConfig` and `OllamaTaskSpec` readers preserve earlier reader meanings;
`read_driver_config` and `read_task_spec` select only declared supported versions.
ProviderProfile stays 2.0; worker results stay 2.3 and are named explicitly by
the 2.4 packet. Executable history requires format 5, not an implicit upgrade.

Only numeric HTTP loopback local fixtures or direct `https://ollama.com` cloud
fixtures are representable. A closed inline synthetic observation binds exact
availability, origin, model, route and auth predicates. Current start and
provider-lookup decisions must both satisfy the unchanged original binding,
with separate exact-mode approved evidence over one context/trust/time snapshot.
Each contributing lookup observation references the exact canonical capture.
Registration and matching blob presence grant no authority; revocation or
expiry at preparation, dispatch or gate release prevents target execution.

The same Claude driver and lifecycle simulate the selected route without a
network request. Local uses a nonsecret placeholder, cloud a closed fixture
reference; real credentials, inherited proxies/model overrides, settings
discovery, model/server operations and fallback are absent. Remote cancellation,
real accounting, native resume, hard cost/token enforcement and production
remain unsupported. See the [provider ADR](adr/0006-ollama-fixture-profiles.md).

## Claude fixture contracts v2.3

The explicit 2.3 family contains `driver-config`, `task-spec`, `worker-packet`,
`packet-projection` and `worker-result`. Earlier schema resources and readers
retain their exact bytes and meanings. `read_task_spec` selects the declared
version; no version or adapter is inferred. A 2.3 task names
`execution.binding_digest` and `execution.driver_config_digest`; it never puts a
DriverConfig digest in a legacy RuntimeProfile field. The separately retained
2.0 ProviderProfile supplies the exact simulated model/provider/auth identities.
The five schemas are available with `schema(name, version="2.3")`.

The trusted `configure_execution` API accepts `driver_config=...` instead of
`runtime_profile_digest` for the explicit `claude-print-fixture/1` projection.
It requires a format-4-or-later store and the same exact installation, binding, policies,
trusted receipts, evidence and context as 2.2 admission. The effective-context
digest binds `{policies: <documents sorted by digest>, driver_config_digest: ...}`.
It admits only installation `synthetic-claude-1`, empty additional instructions,
semantic tool `claude.edit`, the synthetic worker/check backends and no hard
cost/token cap. Provider metadata describes a simulation, never actual routing.
Configuration registration does not authorize a task or enable production.

The owned supervisor emits one canonical 2.3 packet, the identical stdin wire
packet and a mapping binding configuration/provider/admission/session identities.
The session UUID equals the new attempt UUID. Decoder results bind all those
identities; terminal reports are untrusted. Complete owned cessation precedes
candidate freezing and independent verification with a separate genuine v1
check profile. Existing 2.2 result/capabilities envelopes also describe 2.3 tasks
without exposing private paths, policy bodies or credential data.

Native resume refuses. Explicit restart creates a new attempt/session, keeps
worktree fencing and consumes the persisted budget; reported token/cost counters
remain unknown totals. No fallback, public registry release or real vendor
execution is enabled. See the [driver ADR](adr/0005-claude-fixture-driver.md) and
[wire component](claude-protocol.md) for exact limits.

## Single-step execution v2.2

Explicit version `2.2` adds TaskSpecV2, WorkerPacketV2, ExecutionEvidence,
InstructionBundle, ToolPolicy, SandboxPolicy and CheckBinding through
`taskalong.execution`. It also adds closed packet-projection, result-view and
capabilities-view schemas. Use `schema(name, version="2.2")`,
`seal_versioned(name, data, version="2.2")` and `read_task_spec(data)` explicitly.
The v1 reader remains unchanged; reading a saved v1 task preserves its canonical
bytes/digest. The exact 2.0 and 2.1 resource sets and semantics remain unchanged.

A v2 TaskSpec selects `execution.binding_digest`. Its worker and verifier policies
are separate exact immutable references. PolicyResolver accepts only a bounded
operator-selected tuple of typed documents and resolves exact digest plus type.
It does no filesystem/network discovery and grants no authority. Instruction
content and configured runtime paths stay private. A valid schema or self-hash
does not establish effective enforcement, trusted qualification or a launch route.

`RunService.configure_execution(...)` is a trusted operating-system control-plane
API, separate from task submission. It requires explicit installation, provider,
binding, policy, exact runtime-profile digest, context, receipts, approved trust
and evidence bytes. Its 2.2 projection is `codex-v1-fixture/1`: an
explicitly registered synthetic executable and independent fixture verifier
launcher. Empty additional instructions, exactly `fixture.edit`, denied discovery
and the `synthetic-fixture` sandbox backend are its closed policy subset. Legacy
permission objects and extra toolchain roots must be empty; additional constraints
cannot be silently discarded by this projection. These
are simulation inputs, with no claim of actual Codex or OS policy enforcement.
The effective-context digest is SHA-256 of the canonical array of policy documents
sorted by their content digests. Other context identities remain explicit inputs
to the fixture measurement, never proof of this release's runtime qualification.
Requested provider/model/auth identities remain recorded as simulated route
inputs; actual transport is the registered local fixture. Arbitrary policies,
unknown drivers, unresolved documents, non-null cost/token limits and unsupported
native resume are typed refusals. Nothing selects a fallback transport or model.

V2 executable state requires an explicit format-3 store upgrade. Admission
re-evaluates current trusted approvals, expiry/revocation, exact required mode,
profile identity and budgets. A start receipt cannot satisfy a binding requiring
native resume. Preparation atomically retains authority/policy/binding/decision
snapshots, lease, reservation, event and intent. Dispatch and the owned pre-exec
gate revalidate current mutable facts. An interruption after dispatch can leave
unknown effects; the workspace stays quarantined until explicitly reconciled.

The canonical packet binds the 2.2 task and admission. The explicitly projected
v1 wire packet and final mapping bind both packet identities to one attempt.
Legacy worker output must match those exact wire inputs. Independent check
records retain the existing acceptance interpreter and immutable 2.2 evidence
projections. Worker completion does not grant independent acceptance.

`RunService.capabilities(run_id, mode="start")` and `result(run_id)` return 2.2
dictionary envelopes without preparing work, reconciling state or issuing
authority. V1 `inspect`, other dictionary returns, CLI verbs and exit meanings
remain available. V2 start/restart returns its original prepared operation receipt
on both first call and replay; call `inspect` for the latest run revision.
Capabilities reports scoped fixture satisfaction separately from production
dispatch, which is always false. Result distinguishes pending, unknown, completed
worker and independent acceptance, and exposes immutable artifact identities
without policy bodies, configured paths, authority records or raw output. These
views do not authorize execution or publication.

See the [admission ADR](adr/0004-single-step-execution-admission.md) and
[maintenance operations](operations.md#v2-execution-store-boundary).

Persistent stores belong to the `taskalong` application namespace. New stores
record that marker; existing untagged or foreign stores fail before journal-mode
configuration. No automatic cross-application migration is provided.

The importable facade is `taskalong.api.RunService`. Orchestrators call this facade
rather than importing the runtime adapter or interpreting provider output. The
CLI calls that same boundary. `python -m taskalong` and the console script have the
same semantics. Help and version require no state, repository or network access.
Read-only status and events never launch or reconcile a run implicitly.
Repository/profile registration, `configure_review`, `configure_command_sandbox`,
`configure_publication`, and `authorize` are additional trusted control-plane
methods. Their CLI counterparts operate as the current OS user. Task documents
and worker output cannot invoke them or admit their own authority. Authority
records identify that OS principal and retain `human_decision_observed=false`;
no human approval is inferred from an identity string.

Version `1.0` contains exactly these twelve offline Draft 2020-12 schemas:
`task-spec`, `task-run`, `run-event`, `worker-packet`, `worker-result`,
`execution-observation`, `evidence`, `acceptance`, `authority`, `effect-intent`,
`command-result`, and `runtime-profile`. Their IDs are
`urn:taskalong:schema:v1:<name>`. Unknown root/nested contract fields and unsupported
versions fail. Explicit metadata mappings (`extensions`, event payloads, private
profile policy, summary records) are bounded and grant no authority. Extensions
use namespaced keys. There is no remote schema resolution.

The JSON boundary rejects duplicate keys, invalid UTF-8, floats/non-finite
numbers, excessive nesting and inputs over 1 MiB. Integers stay within the
interoperable 53-bit JSON range. Schema integer fields reject booleans. Goals and
non-goals together are limited to 16 KiB. Literal POSIX scope rejects traversal,
absolute paths, globs, symlinks, Git/control/agent configuration and credentials.
The core separately checks actual file bytes, mode and scope before acceptance.
Required checks use argv and expected exit zero; shell strings are unsupported.

Canonical bytes are validated normalized UTF-8 JSON with sorted object keys,
compact separators, `ensure_ascii=False`, no implicit Unicode normalization and
no floating point. SHA-256 excludes only the root's own `digest` field. Set-like
scope, effect, criterion and evidence lists are sorted/deduplicated at admission;
semantic arrays such as argv retain order. A changed semantic input changes the
digest. IDs and human-readable names grant no authority.

Frozen document types in `taskalong.contracts` store canonical bytes. `from_dict`
validates; `to_dict` returns an independent copy. Runtime protocol records live
in `taskalong.executors.base`; they carry no acceptance or publishing capability.
The protocol names provider-neutral start/status/cancel/resume operations, while
this first adapter requires `RunService` to own their durable lifecycle.
`CodexCLI.start` and `.resume` return the unsupported `supervisor_required`
observation. Its internal `.run` primitive is called only by the owned per-run
supervisor after attempt/effect preparation. Direct adapter method presence is
not standalone execution support; callers use `RunService` for execution,
reconciliation, lookup and cancellation.
Worker output is untrusted, including fields claiming commands passed or a person
approved them. Only an actual independent owned invocation can produce trusted
command/review evidence. A missing reviewer, partial coverage or stale subject
blocks acceptance.

Mutations accept operation keys and expected run revisions. A repeated key with
the same semantic request returns its prior receipt before checking optimistic
revision. A repeated key with different semantics conflicts. State changes and
consecutive events commit atomically; sequence establishes ordering. Read-only
portable summaries omit private runtime thread IDs and absolute control paths.
Exports omit raw prompts, source, results, credentials and logs by default.

The lifecycle is `created → ready → running → verifying → accepted → publishing
→ draft_published`, with typed blocked/failure/cancellation states. A worker
completion starts verification. Only exact current independent evidence can
produce acceptance; publication needs additional exact intent authority.
Terminal cancellation/failure cannot be silently resumed. Unknown spawn,
cancellation or remote effects require reconciliation rather than duplicate
execution. Native resume names an observed session and never means latest-session
or restart. Unsupported native resume cannot silently fall back to another mode.

Cancellation confirmation is selected from the state observed inside the
completion transaction, including a request made after the worker returns.
Stale blockers cannot reopen terminal cancellation. A cancellation before any
dispatch can be reconciled without launching a worker; unresolved invocation
effects still prevent confirmation. Native resume rejects a different returned
session identity. Reported input/output token usage accumulates across attempts;
an unknown component or integer overflow leaves the corresponding total unknown.
Provider cost remains unknown.

Explicit `retire-workspace` / `RunService.retire_workspace` releases a quiescent
terminal or accepted run's repository reservation after cessation and effect
checks. It preserves retained data, records `workspace.retired` and revokes the
old fence. A new task receives a distinct workspace and increasing generation;
retired runs cannot regain mutation authority. See [operations](operations.md).

Candidate effect intents journal bounded file metadata rather than base64 source
bytes. Existing inline-content intents remain readable and content-checked;
current source limits remain one MiB per file and eight MiB per candidate.

Production profiles always fail preflight with `runtime_policy_unsupported`.
The missing qualification covers effective exec config/instruction/tool discovery
and the complete no-daemon worker lifetime. Profile qualification receipt IDs
are not proof and cannot turn this gate on. Synthetic fixtures remain explicitly
synthetic throughout the lifecycle; no live executor support is claimed.

For worker/check cessation, Darwin's `darwin-kqueue-no-fork` backend treats every
observed fork as unaccounted descendants and blocks advancement. Linux's
`linux-child-subreaper` backend uses an isolated non-dumpable wrapper and private
status pipe to report root termination and kernel child reaping. Linux generic
process-backend qualification awaits actual matching CI and installed tests.
Even passing those tests does not qualify a real CLI: production also requires
separate effective instruction/tool and complete owned-runtime proof. An expired
heartbeat, process-list snapshot, closed pipe or delivered signal cannot replace
that receipt. Git publication transport may use verified process-group exit
plus exact remote read-back; this does not grant worker/check quiescence.

The implementation is original; no source from unrelated projects is imported.
The source import allowlist is empty. The tested dependency floor is
`jsonschema>=4.26,<5`, with exact qualification versions/hashes in the lockfile;
Python/platform support still requires recorded environment-specific evidence.

JSON CLI results have one `command_result` envelope; events JSONL is the explicit
exception. `ok` describes the command, not task acceptance. Exit codes are:

| Exit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Command fulfilled; task may still be blocked in a read-only observation. |
| 1 | Known execution or verification failure. |
| 2 | CLI, schema or input validation error. |
| 3 | Blocked prerequisite, missing authority/review, unsupported capability. |
| 4 | Revision, key or lease conflict. |
| 5 | Unknown effect; reconciliation required. |
| 6 | Pending after bounded wait. |
| 70 | Internal/store integrity error; preserve state. |
| 130 | Foreground client interrupted; does not imply worker cancellation. |

No live task-to-verified-draft-PR, exactly-once remote effect, hard provider cost
cap, arbitrary-runtime compatibility, public license or release claim follows
from these contracts.

## Offline semantic documents v2

`taskalong.bindings.HarnessInstallation`, `ProviderProfile` and `ExecutionBinding`
are frozen canonical documents using schema version `2.0`. Their three schemas
have IDs `urn:taskalong:schema:v2:<name>`. They are descriptive data only: no
registration, trusted resolution, DB migration, task v2, driver selection or
production admission is implemented here. Existing v1 APIs, canonical bytes,
digests and schema resources keep their original behavior.

```python
from importlib import resources
from taskalong.bindings import HarnessInstallation
from taskalong.validation import schema, schema_names, validate_versioned

assert len(schema_names()) == 12  # Existing default remains v1.
assert len(schema_names(version="2.0")) == 3
resource = resources.files("taskalong.resources").joinpath(
    "examples", "v2", "harness-installation.json")
installation = HarnessInstallation(resource.read_bytes())
document = validate_versioned("harness-installation", installation.to_dict(),
                              expected_version="2.0")
assert schema("harness-installation", version="2.0")["additionalProperties"] is False
```

The installed `examples/v2/` directory also contains `provider-profile.json` and
`execution-binding.json`. Each example is complete, sealed and synthetic. The
binding links the other two example digests. Its policy/check references and
runtime/model digests are synthetic declarations, not existing approved objects
or evidence. They cannot admit a launch. The provider example names loopback but
does not connect to it or claim any server/model is installed.

`seal_versioned(name, data, version="2.0")` supplies kind/version and seals strict
JSON. `validate_versioned(..., expected_version=...)` requires the caller's
selected format; it never guesses from input. Version `1.0` uses the existing
validator/sealer unchanged. Schema enumeration and registries are explicitly
version-scoped, installed and offline. Frozen `from_dict` and byte constructors
validate, `to_dict` returns an independent copy, and `to_bytes` returns canonical
bytes. Unknown fields/versions, malformed digests, duplicate keys, non-integer
numbers, overflow and recognizable credentials are rejected. Sensitive-input
screening is a secondary check, not arbitrary secret detection.

Installation identity includes harness, adapter/driver and CLI versions, exact
platform/backend, executable digest and a separate dependency-closure digest.
Paths and arbitrary argv/imports are absent. Unknown adapter IDs can be stored as
design data but are unavailable to the unchanged closed registry. A declared
closure hash does not prove that the complete executable closure was captured.

Provider profiles have closed harness/provider/auth variants for Codex account,
Claude account/API, separate Claude/Ollama local and cloud destinations, Cursor
account and Antigravity account. Model requested identity and resolved digest,
endpoint, credential reference, effort/tier and auxiliary profile references are
explicit semantic inputs. Account/API references are nonsecret identifiers, never
secret values or credential file paths. Local Ollama requires an HTTP(S) literal
loopback endpoint and local-no-secret auth; other variants require HTTPS and an
explicit credential/account reference. Userinfo, query/fragment, invalid ports
and control characters are refused. Endpoint validation performs no DNS lookup.
Loopback does not prove local computation, effective egress or routing. A model
digest is a declaration requiring later trusted evidence, not alias resolution.
Unlisted auxiliary routes and fallback are forbidden. Supported data variants
and option names make no claim that a corresponding installed CLI accepts them.

Bindings reference installation/provider, instruction/tool policy, worker sandbox
and independent check-binding digests. Complete policy records and trusted
resolvers belong to a later milestone. No qualification receipt field exists;
receipt rotation therefore cannot change binding identity. Capabilities form a
nonempty unique set sorted before hashing. Auxiliary routes retain declared
order. Budgets use integer seconds/tokens/micro-USD; null is unspecified, not zero
usage or spending authority. A required hard cap needs a numeric limit and its
required capability; declaring it still proves no enforcement.

Native resume is null unless explicitly required. Its protocol version,
`exact_stored_session` scope and compatibility digest bind every semantic binding
input (including policies, independent check binding, required capabilities and
budgets). `native_resume_compatibility_digest` computes this identity excluding
only the two digest fields themselves. Use the complete kind/version-bearing
document as input. Altering any compatibility subject requires a new digest.
No session is transferred or resumed by these records; later admission must also
verify the exact stored session, evidence and fresh authority.

Future milestones must preserve these shipped v2 bytes/meanings or introduce an
explicit new schema version/discriminant. Neither v1 nor v2 authority may be
silently reinterpreted. Production refusal remains in force.

## Offline qualification v2.1

`taskalong.qualification` adds frozen `QualificationReceipt`,
`QualificationDecision` and `CapabilityReport` records. Read them with explicit
version `2.1`; its schema IDs use `urn:taskalong:schema:v2.1:<name>`. Existing
v1 defaults and M1's exact v2.0 enumeration, schemas and canonical examples remain
unchanged. Shared subject, observation, evidence-reference and trust-policy
shapes are embedded in the receipt schema and resolve only in the offline 2.1
registry. These records do not register profiles or change runtime admission.

`evaluate` takes M1 binding/installation/provider records, explicit context and
operation mode, receipts, a `TrustPolicy`, an immutable `EvidenceStore`, explicit
UTC evaluation time and a minimum evidence level. The default minimum is
`actual_provider`; fixture and controlled-responder evidence cannot satisfy it.
No callback resolver, filesystem search, network connection, clock lookup,
credential discovery, process, persistence or launch is performed. Installed
schema resources are read-only package constants. Evidence snapshots are bounded
to 128 blobs, one MiB each and 16 MiB total; receipts are bounded to 64 per call.
Strict JSON and output size limits still apply; excessive output fails closed.

Trusted policy is an external control-plane input. Its constructor validates
shape and digests, not origin or authorization. Applications must supply it from
authenticated operator-approved evidence; never construct approvals from worker,
profile, task or receipt claims. Producer-name matching alone is insufficient:
an exact receipt digest needs a current, unrevoked trusted approval. That approval
is sealed after the receipt exists, so receipts do not refer back to approvals.
Producer evidence-level restrictions and current receipt/approval/evidence
revocations are separately checked. The caller must supply trusted current time
and a current policy snapshot. This module implements no signer, key store or
approval acquisition.

Each receipt binds exact semantic binding/installation/provider, artifact,
runtime closure, host/backend, model, instruction/tool/worker/check policy,
effective context and test inputs. Native resume additionally binds exact session,
prior invocation and M1 compatibility identity. Mode is separate: start evidence
never implicitly grants observe, cancellation, result, resume, provider lookup or
remote cancellation. The decision requires every binding-required capability plus
the operation's mandatory capability, all under that exact mode. Native-resume
observations are eligible only in native-resume mode, where both session and
prior-invocation identities are mandatory. Requiring resume in a binding cannot
turn start-mode evidence into resume support. Missing evidence
stays unknown; explicit negative facts stay unsupported. Conflicting trusted
negative/unknown results cannot be overwritten by positive results. Untrusted or
invalid extra records are rejected and recorded without supplying votes.

Evidence references bind SHA-256, size, media type and public/private
classification. Approved typed observation manifests bind their producer,
subject/mode/level/capability, expected support and observed boolean/null facts.
They must link available, matching raw captures. False is unsupported; null is
unknown. A root exit without complete descendant proof cannot report local
cessation. Local proof does not imply provider acknowledgment, remote work stop
or final accounting. Hard token/cost guarantees need complete facts for every
route, enforcement before dispatch, overrun prevention and the exact declared
limit; cost additionally needs a known billing bound. Insufficient hard-cap proof
returns unsupported. These are checks of approved evidence declarations and
capture identity, not independent proof that a producer's claims are truthful.
Trusted capture/approval provenance and real runtime campaigns remain necessary.

The decision records the trusted policy digest, verified receipt digests,
rejected input indices/reason codes and scoped outcomes. A report links that
decision, retains receipt limitations and individual nullable usage, and never
invents aggregate token/cost totals. No raw capture bytes are copied into outputs.
Rotation creates a new decision while preserving binding identity and old bytes.
Both returned records always carry `production_dispatch_allowed=false`, including
a satisfied actual-provider-level input decision. Existing production preflight
is unchanged and cannot be enabled by any of these records.

The installed `examples/v2.1/` bundle is a complete generated offline example:
three sealed records, a narrow M1 binding fixture, an observation/capture and an
explicit fixture-only trust policy. Its synthetic digests/approval are not real
runtime evidence. This example trusts only those fixed generated inputs:

```python
import hashlib
from importlib import resources
from taskalong.bindings import ExecutionBinding, HarnessInstallation, ProviderProfile
from taskalong.qualification import EvidenceStore, QualificationReceipt, TrustPolicy, evaluate

root = resources.files("taskalong.resources")
example = root.joinpath("examples/v2.1")
binding = ExecutionBinding(example.joinpath("binding-fixture.json").read_bytes())
installation = HarnessInstallation(root.joinpath("examples/v2/harness-installation.json").read_bytes())
provider = ProviderProfile(root.joinpath("examples/v2/provider-profile.json").read_bytes())
receipt = QualificationReceipt(example.joinpath("qualification-receipt.json").read_bytes())
trust = TrustPolicy(example.joinpath("trust-policy.json").read_bytes())
blobs = {}
for name in ("evidence-observation.json", "capture.txt"):
    raw = example.joinpath(name).read_bytes()
    blobs[hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()] = raw
context = {key: receipt.to_dict()["subject"][key] for key in (
    "artifact_digest", "host_digest", "effective_context_digest", "test_inputs_digest",
    "session_digest", "prior_invocation_digest")}
result = evaluate(binding, installation=installation, provider=provider,
    context=context, mode="start", receipts=[receipt], trust=trust,
    evidence=EvidenceStore.from_blobs(blobs), now="2026-10-22T12:00:00Z",
    minimum_level="offline_fixture")  # Explicit fixture scope only.
assert result.decision.to_dict()["requirements_satisfied"]
assert result.report.to_dict()["production_dispatch_allowed"] is False
```

The bundled binding remains a v2.0 document; the directory groups this example,
not a redefinition of M1. The supplied time is a fixture constant, not a current
approval. Real callers must use trusted current time and evidence. M3 persistence,
M4 admission, live adapters, effective-policy proof and runtime enablement are
separate milestones.

```python
response = root / "review-response.json"
response.write_text('{"summary":"Generated fixture review.","comments":[]}\n')

service = RunService(root / "state")
registration = service.register_repository(repo, root / "workspaces")
profile = service.register_profile({
    "profile_id": "generated-fixture", "qualification": "synthetic", "adapter": "codex-cli",
    "executable_path": str(worker), "executable_sha256": hashlib.sha256(worker.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
    "runtime_version": "0.163.0", "model": "gpt-6.1-sol", "reasoning_effort": "high", "service_tier": "default",
    "inference_destination_id": "generated-local-fixture", "permission_policy": {},
    "permission_policy_digest": digest({}), "toolchain_read_roots": [],
    "credential_source_ref": None, "qualification_receipt_ids": []})
service.configure_command_sandbox(launcher)
service.configure_review(config, fixture_response=response, executable=reviewer,
                         python_executable=sys.executable)

def submit(name):
    task = {
        "task_id": name, "revision": 1, "goal": "Correct addition in the generated fixture.",
        "non_goals": ["No network, dependencies, publication, or other source changes."],
        "repository": {"registration_id": registration["registration_id"], "base_commit": base, "base_ref": "main"},
        "scope": {"files": ["arithmetic.py"], "operations": ["modify"]},
        "criteria": [{"id": "sum", "description": "Addition returns 5.", "check_ids": ["sum-check"]}],
        "checks": [{"id": "sum-check", "argv": [sys.executable, "-B", "check.py"], "cwd": ".",
                    "timeout_seconds": 10, "expected_exit_code": 0, "criterion_ids": ["sum"], "required": True}],
        "execution": {"adapter": "codex-cli", "profile_id": profile["profile_id"], "profile_digest": profile["digest"]},
        "permissions": {"local_edit": True, "local_commit": True, "inference_destination_id": profile["inference_destination_id"],
                        "allowed_effects": ["execute", "verify", "commit_candidate"]},
        "budget": {"max_attempts": 2, "attempt_seconds": 5 if name == "recovery-example" else 15, "total_active_seconds": 60,
                   "max_output_bytes": 1048576, "hard_cost_usd": None, "hard_tokens": None},
        "review": {"required": True, "integration": "reviewsensei", "contract": "0.8.8/v1",
                   "config_digest": hashlib.sha256(config.read_bytes()).hexdigest(), "require_full_coverage": True},
        "publication": None, "qualification": "synthetic"}
    run = service.submit(task, operation_key="submit-" + name)
    authority = service.authorize(run["run_id"], decision_digest=run["spec_digest"],
                                  scope=["execute", "verify", "commit_candidate"], qualification="synthetic")
    service.start(run["run_id"], operation_key="start-" + name, expected_revision=run["revision"],
                  authority_id=authority["authority_id"])
    return run["run_id"]

def wait(run_id, states=("accepted", "blocked", "cancelled", "failed")):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 45
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        run = service.inspect(run_id)
        if run["state"] in states:
            return run
        time.sleep(.05)
    raise RuntimeError("Inspect the preserved run; do not retry an uncertain effect")

def retire(run):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
    while True:
        try:
            return service.retire_workspace(run["run_id"], operation_key="retire-" + run["run_id"],
                                            expected_revision=run["revision"])
        except TaskAlongError as error:
            if error.code not in {"supervisor_owned", "operation_in_progress"} or time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                raise
            time.sleep(.05)  # Only a proven no-effect guard conflict may retry.

first = wait(submit("accepted-example"))
assert first["state"] == "accepted", first["blockers"]
retire(first)

mode("hang")
recovery = wait(submit("recovery-example"))
assert recovery["state"] == "blocked" and not recovery["active_attempt_id"]
recovery = service.reconcile(recovery["run_id"], operation_key="reconcile-example", expected_revision=recovery["revision"])
mode("good")
service.resume(recovery["run_id"], mode="native", operation_key="native-example", expected_revision=recovery["revision"])
recovery = wait(recovery["run_id"])
assert recovery["state"] == "accepted" and len(recovery["attempts"]) == 2
retire(recovery)

mode("hang")
cancel_id = submit("cancel-example")
running = wait(cancel_id, states=("running",))
service.cancel(cancel_id, operation_key="cancel-example", expected_revision=running["revision"])
cancelled = wait(cancel_id, states=("cancelled", "blocked"))
assert cancelled["state"] == "cancelled", cancelled["blockers"]
retire(cancelled)

mode("good")
interactive = wait(submit("inspect-example"))
assert interactive["state"] == "accepted", interactive["blockers"]
print(json.dumps({"state_dir": str(root / "state"), "run_id": interactive["run_id"],
                  "revision": interactive["revision"], "state": interactive["state"],
                  "qualification": interactive["qualification"]}, indent=2))
service.close()
```

The first candidate reaches acceptance only after its independent command and
released fixture review pass. The recovery task times out, reconciles, and uses
the recorded native thread with a new attempt and fence. The cancellation task
requests cancellation and waits for confirmed local cessation. Retirement admits
the next task while retaining the old workspace and evidence. No publication is
configured or permitted.

Use the printed state directory, run ID and current revision with the CLI:

```sh
taskalong --state-dir STATE_DIR status RUN_ID --json
taskalong --state-dir STATE_DIR events RUN_ID --jsonl
GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 taskalong --state-dir STATE_DIR verify RUN_ID --key fresh-verification --expected-revision REVISION --json
```

For this generated fixture only, the verification command uses the same
process-scoped Git configuration as the example. It does not change host
configuration. Existing user repositories must satisfy their own qualified
Git policy; do not use these overrides to bypass that policy.

Always inspect status before a new mutation, and use a fresh key for new intent.
Repeating the same key returns its original receipt, even if the run later changes.
Do not change a submitted task's budget or profile to make a failed attempt pass.
The 1 MiB output budget covers worker output, result files, checks, reviewer
schema/version probes, and review output; a tiny 64 KiB total may not fund review.

For the standard foreground CLI, Ctrl-C during `verify` returns exit 130. Inspect
the resulting `verification_interrupted` error and run. Confirmed cleanup leaves
a blocked run whose capture is observed; a fresh verification key can continue.
Unknown cessation leaves an unknown pending effect and requires reconciliation;
do not clear it from the database or infer cessation from process absence. An
earlier process crash with no durable receipt remains uncertain after upgrading.
Interrupting a foreground client of a detached worker does not cancel that worker;
use `cancel` and observe `cancel.confirmed`. If verification finished before the
keypress, report the state actually committed rather than claiming interruption.

# Local operations

Use the installed console script or `python -m taskalong`. The CLI's `--help` is
the authoritative command syntax for this experimental foundation. Start with version
and model-free doctor output; missing credentials, authorization, compatible
profile, containment or reviewer remain typed blockers. Doctor never logs in,
installs a runtime, edits personal configuration or launches inference.
Production start/resume currently fail preflight with
`runtime_policy_unsupported` for every production profile. Full effective exec
configuration/instruction/tool discovery and owned `--no-daemon` worker lifetime
remain unqualified; a passing no-model command probe or operator-supplied receipt
ID does not remove this gate. Synthetic test profiles exercise the implemented
core without enabling live source transmission.

State belongs outside repositories and site-packages. Linux defaults to
`$XDG_STATE_HOME/taskalong` (absolute paths only) or `~/.local/state/taskalong`;
macOS defaults to `~/Library/Application Support/TaskAlong`. An explicit operator
state directory must be private, owned by the current OS user and have no
symlinked control paths. On macOS, resolve an operating-system temporary-root
alias before selecting a scratch state directory. Never chmod an existing shared
directory to make it pass. Local filesystems and one trusted OS operator are the
supported model; multi-user stores and network shares are unsupported.

New stores carry the `application=taskalong` metadata tag. Untagged or foreign
application stores are rejected with `unsupported_store_application`; do not
relabel them to bypass this check. This candidate does not import or migrate
another installation's stores, worktrees or sessions. Preserve those records
and use their owning application. TaskAlong uses its own state/control paths.

The state store uses SQLite WAL, foreign keys, full synchronous transactions and
bounded busy waits. A transaction advances one run revision and appends its
ordered events together. Content-addressed blobs are durable before references
commit. Missing or tampered referenced blobs block recovery/acceptance; orphaned
blobs remain preserved. Never reset a corrupt store, discard its event history,
or relabel a future format to run older code. Use SQLite's backup API rather than
copying only a live database file without its WAL.

Repository registration binds its canonical Git common directory to one state
store. A common-directory OS lock serializes admission and a lease fences mutable
work. Keep the primary checkout clean and unchanged. TaskAlong retains owned marked
worktrees and branches after completion and never stashes, resets, adopts foreign
work or performs automatic cleanup. Do not remove its live lock file. Dirty or
foreign workspaces and unknown processes require operator reconciliation.

After a cancelled, failed, accepted or draft-published run is quiescent, the
operator can release repository exclusivity explicitly:

```sh
taskalong --state-dir /absolute/private/state retire-workspace RUN_ID \
  --expected-revision REVISION --key unique-retirement-key --json
```

`RunService.retire_workspace` provides the same operation. Retirement requires
all operation guards, no active attempt or unresolved effect, confirmed cessation
for every recorded invocation, and the matching workspace fence. An accepted run
also requires its exact candidate. It records `workspace.retired` and revokes the
old fence while preserving the worktree, branch, marker, evidence and history.
A later task receives a fresh workspace and a greater repository generation.
The retired run cannot resume, verify or publish; this operation does not delete
data or release an uncertain process. Repeating the same key returns its original
retirement receipt.

Worker tools and verifier commands need the qualified named command sandbox.
The Codex parent may use already authorized runtime authentication; child tools
must not read private control state or credential paths, change Git metadata,
write outside the exact workspace, or access network. A missing sandbox capability
blocks execution. Inference source disclosure remains a separate operator grant
from disabling tool network access. Runtime session retention is owned by Codex;
TaskAlong does not delete or migrate those sessions.

Submit creates immutable task state without launching work. Start requires
separately admitted local-effect/inference authority. Status is read-only. Cancel
records a request; only owned-process cessation can confirm local cancellation.
An outer CLI interruption does not stop a detached supervisor. A stale heartbeat
or numeric PID alone never authorizes killing or reusing a process/workspace.
Reconcile is an explicit mutation and can remain uncertain. On Darwin, the
kernel exit/fork observer only confirms non-forking lifetimes: any observed fork
quarantines the invocation. Linux uses a separate non-dumpable child subreaper
and target-inaccessible status pipe; root exit plus kernel child reaping is its
cessation boundary. Linux support is pending exact-head CI and installed
qualification. Missing or lost lifetime receipts remain uncertain on either
platform. Native resume requires
the observed thread, compatible task/profile/content, fresh attempt/fence and
remaining persisted budget; restart is separately explicit. Provider cost and
remote billing cessation can remain unknown after local process death.

The standard foreground `verify` CLI defers Ctrl-C while it collects the owned
process cleanup receipt and persists the capture outcome, then returns exit 130
with `verification_interrupted`. Confirmed cleanup leaves a blocked run that can
be inspected and verified with a fresh key, accounting for actual captured bytes.
Unconfirmed descendants keep the effect unknown and the workspace reserved. This
does not repair an older interrupted effect with no durable receipt, and a process
crash/SIGKILL can still require quarantine. Custom caller signal handlers retain
their own semantics. Interrupting a client of a detached worker still does not
cancel that worker; use the explicit cancellation operation.

The [installed fixture walkthrough](fixture-walkthrough.md) is also available as
`taskalong guide`. Synthetic command launchers require explicit `configure-sandbox`
admission and make no containment claim. Reviewer setup should select both the
reviewer executable and its Python interpreter from the intended installed venv.
A missing executable returns `review_executable_missing` with an actionable
prerequisite rather than a local-store failure.

Independent verification rechecks exact content before and after each check and
released ReviewSensei invocation. Worker command claims cannot satisfy criteria.
Only full current released review coverage plus all required checks can accept.
A synthetic fixture result is labeled synthetic through acceptance and can never
authorize production publication. A missing optional ReviewSensei installation
blocks required review rather than weakening the acceptance policy.

Use `RunService` or its CLI for start/status/cancel/resume/reconcile. Direct
`CodexCLI.start` and `.resume` return `supervisor_required`; the actual bounded
`.run` driver belongs beneath the durable per-run supervisor. Registration,
profile/configuration and `authorize` commands are privileged OS control-plane
operations. They record the current OS principal and
`human_decision_observed=false`; they do not authenticate a person from a supplied
name or worker claim. Synthetic sandbox/transport settings cannot enable a
production TaskSpec.

Publish-intent displays exact candidate, evidence, repository/base, branch, title,
body and draft payload. An explicit publish invocation with that intent digest
admits the exact effect from the trusted OS operator. It does not authenticate a
self-declared human name. Git branch creation uses an expected-absent lease;
existing foreign refs block. PR discovery searches all states with a stable run
marker. Unknown responses are reconciled by read-only lookup, never blind POST
retries. Publisher Git transport checks process-group exit plus protocol and
remote read-back. That narrower transport observation cannot establish
worker/check quiescence, authorize a pending worker effect, or release a
quarantined lease. Rollback/cancellation does not delete or close a branch or PR.

Default export is redacted metadata. Raw prompts, source, reviews, runtime handles,
private paths and logs are private artifacts and are not automatically included.
Input screening/redaction is a secondary defense with documented limits, not a
claim to detect arbitrary secrets. No telemetry, automatic retention deletion,
legacy store discovery, credential setup or package registry upload occurs.

Rollback means stop/reconcile owned processes, disable new starts if a profile
fails, preserve unknown processes/worktrees/state, and reinstall the last reviewed
qualified wheel using a separate scratch state directory if needed. Reverting
source does not undo external effects. Licensing, per-file extraction rights,
public notices, live qualification and public release remain separate owner gates.
Application code/resources/fixtures are original; the source import allowlist
remains empty. The [MIT License](../LICENSE) includes the owner-approved copyright notice.
The runtime dependency floor is `jsonschema>=4.26,<5`, reflecting the exercised
version; use the exact hashed qualification lock when replaying evidence.
See [contracts](contracts.md), [provenance](provenance.json) and
[qualification](qualification.md) for exact boundaries and evidence.

## Quiescent store maintenance

Database format 2 adds immutable installation/provider/binding/decision history.
It is independent of document schema versions. New stores still use format 1;
ordinary opening never silently upgrades an existing store. Original v1 records
and the original legacy profiles remain unchanged.

Close all Store/RunService clients and allow owned invocations to stop and their
effects to reconcile before maintenance. Current clients hold a lifetime shared
gate; maintenance requires its exclusive gate and actual SQLite exclusive
ownership in rollback-journal mode. An open predecessor WAL client prevents that
transition. `maintenance_busy`, `maintenance_exclusivity_unproven` or
`maintenance_not_quiescent` is a refusal, not permission to ignore a lock or kill
an unverified PID. Unknown effect kinds, inconsistent records and uncertain
cessation remain blocked. Only local filesystems and a trusted OS operator are
supported. A new advisory file alone cannot fence older clients.

Qualification checks exact predecessor opening before/after maintenance and
refusal of maintenance while that predecessor is active. Separate real SQLite
subprocesses, with only their own retry handlers disabled, must return numeric
BUSY for protected reads and write reservations while maintenance retains its
kernel lock. Unlocked controls and an advisory-only counterexample must succeed
at those operations. These checks preserve logical state and require observed
child completion/reaping. The ten-second probe bound is test containment, not a
product refusal SLA; timeout remains failure. The historical default-handler
constructor timeout is unresolved and its latency is not qualified by this proof.

The trusted Python operator API performs the complete sequence:

```python
from taskalong.store import Store

# All paths are operator-selected private local locations. Backup and restore
# must be new, separate directories outside the original control directory.
with Store.maintenance(state_path) as maintenance:
    receipt = maintenance.upgrade(
        operation_key="history-upgrade-1",
        backup_dir=backup_path,
        restore_dir=restore_verification_path,
    )
```

The durable intent binds the operation key to store identity, target version and
both target paths. A complete control backup and verified fresh restore precede
DDL. OS aliases and case variations cannot make an existing control directory
count as a separate backup or restore destination. Original application-table
rows/digests, blob references, retained captures,
instruction files and required control metadata are included privately. SQLite's
backup captures committed WAL data; copying only state.sqlite3 is insufficient.
SQLite WAL/SHM/rollback journals and empty coordination lock files are omitted
explicitly because the snapshot replaces the journals and OS locks cannot be
restored from bytes. External worktrees/repositories, executables, remote effects
and referenced files outside the control directory require separate preservation
and reconciliation. This is a complete control-state backup, not an environment
or project backup.

Files/directories retain their private modes. Symlinks, hard links, special files,
insecure existing paths, missing/tampered registered or core-evidence blobs and
inconsistent manifests refuse the operation. Existing permissions are never
silently repaired. New attempt containers are created privately; an older store
with shared-mode nested control paths needs explicit operator reconciliation.
Inventories are bounded to 10,000 entries, 64 directory levels, 512 MiB total
payload and the existing bounded JSON manifest size. Exceeding a bound refuses
without deleting partial artifacts.

Migration SQL 002 adds immutable history and atomically commits both schema
markers and its receipt. Matching retries return the committed receipt or verify
and reuse complete pre-migration artifacts. Changed paths/inputs under the same
key conflict. ENOSPC, interrupted copying or incomplete artifacts keep the prior
format and retained failure data; inspect and reconcile rather than overwriting
their destinations. A later source change makes the old backup stale.

For a complete backup without upgrading, use `maintenance.backup(new_path,
complete=True)` inside the same maintenance context. The original
`Store.backup(new_sqlite_path)` API remains a SQLite-only snapshot and is not a
complete control backup or redacted export.

`taskalong.maintenance.verify_backup(path, expected_digest=trusted_digest)` checks
the complete manifest and payload. `restore_backup(path, new_directory,
expected_digest=trusted_digest)` restores only to a fresh directory. The expected
digest must come from the trusted operator's retained receipt, not a worker claim.
Hashes establish identity, not authenticity. Restores are deliberately tagged
`taskalong.restore-quarantine`; current and predecessor clients both refuse them.
The restore is built and verified in a private sibling staging directory with a
canonical quarantine database committed before any payload is copied. Atomic
no-replace directory publication exposes only the complete quarantine at the
selected destination. Unsupported platform/filesystem primitives refuse this
step; a racing existing directory is never replaced, even when empty. Failures
retain private stages for inspection. There is no automatic promotion, in-place
rollback or restore over later effects.
Preserve the original store and reconcile external state before any future
forward-repair procedure. Backups contain private unredacted data: do not put them
in source control, public issues or distribution artifacts.

After upgrade, `Store.record_document(typed_document, operation_key=...)` appends
validated immutable RuntimeProfile, HarnessInstallation, ProviderProfile,
ExecutionBinding or QualificationDecision bytes. `Store.document_history(kind,
identity)` returns frozen records and refuses histories larger than 1,000 entries
instead of returning a partial result. Provider/installation identity uses its
declared ID, bindings use their digest, and decisions use `binding_digest:mode`.
No implicit latest/current selection is provided. Storing or reading a decision
does not grant execution, publication or current qualification authority.

## V2 execution store boundary

Executable 2.2 tasks require store format 3, which deliberately excludes older
clients that cannot enforce v2 restrictions. Ordinary opening, inspection and v1
operation never upgrade a store. After closing all clients and proving quiescence,
use the same complete-backup and quarantined-restore boundary for each numbered
migration. From a format-2 store:

```python
from taskalong.store import Store

with Store.maintenance(state_dir) as store:
    receipt = store.upgrade(
        operation_key="explicit-format3-upgrade",
        backup_dir=new_private_backup_directory,
        restore_dir=new_quarantined_restore_directory,
        target_version=3,
    )
```

A format-1 store must first explicitly complete its existing format-2 migration
with separate backup/restore paths and operation key. SQL001/002, their receipts
and legacy canonical state remain intact. SQL003 adds immutable execution
projection registrations and advances both format markers in one transaction.
Same-key/same-input replay returns its retained receipt; changed inputs conflict.
Failures preserve the source, prior state and private backup/restore evidence.
No downgrade, rollback over later effects or restore promotion is implemented.

After upgrade, trusted local execution configuration stores exact policy history
and an immutable fixture projection. Explicit trust/receipt updates remain
operator settings and are re-evaluated before dispatch; historical decisions never
become current authority. Registering a portable document, opening a store or
reading a result cannot select a model, start inference or enable production.
The [contracts guide](contracts.md#single-step-execution-v22) describes the current
synthetic-only subset and refusal boundaries.

This is an offline developer fixture through the same Claude driver. Select the

# Qualification

This candidate is a fixture-qualified foundation with **production dispatch
disabled**. It does not claim usable live Codex/Claude execution, model review,
provider cancellation, complete runtime isolation or actual GitHub publication.

Candidate receipts are kept by the owner outside the distribution and bind exact
source, interpreter/host versions, artifact, lock and test-input hashes.
Linux-specific lifetime tests are skipped on macOS and require actual Linux
execution; no macOS result qualifies them. Local checks do not qualify a different
hosted OS image. Every intended Python/platform cell needs its own exact-head CI
receipt; matching Python versions alone do not establish platform equivalence.

Maintenance exclusion uses a composed proof: actual byte-pinned predecessor
compatibility and active-client refusal, plus fresh real SQLite subprocesses
that bypass the advisory gate and receive numeric BUSY at the protected read
and write-reservation operations. Only the witnesses use zero busy retry time;
neither the predecessor nor production settings change. Unlocked controls and
an advisory-only counterexample must expose missing kernel exclusion, and
application rows/schema/identities/blob/control inventory must remain unchanged.
The ten-second witness deadline is containment; timeout, wrong/missing evidence,
unrelated errors or unconfirmed cleanup fail qualification. The historical
default busy-handler constructor timeout remains unexplained. The replacement
proves exclusion within the trusted local-filesystem scope, not legacy response
latency, native scheduling behavior or hostile same-user isolation.

```sh
python -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-dev.lock
python -m build --no-isolation --sdist --wheel
python tools/normalize_sdist.py dist/*.tar.gz
python tools/check_dist.py --dist-dir dist
python tools/qualify_installed.py --dist-dir dist --artifact wheel --mode fixture
python tools/qualify_installed.py --dist-dir dist --artifact sdist --mode fixture
python tools/qualify_installed.py --dist-dir dist --artifact wheel --core-only
```

The qualifier creates fresh ordinary environments outside the checkout. Source
reads/import fallback are denied. External synthetic CLI/GitHub fixtures remain
outside the installed wheel. ReviewSensei 0.8.8 is checksum-pinned and uses its
actual released fixture backend; this is not live model review. Synthetic
lost-response publication must reconcile one fixture create. Missing required
review blocks acceptance. These checks produce no runtime authority.

The existing Codex CLI target is 0.163.0. Prior controlled-responder probes did
not establish complete descendant cessation or effective instruction/tool
isolation. Resume must not follow an unconfirmed lifetime. The current Darwin
backend quarantines forks; Linux subreaper tests still do not, by themselves,
qualify a real CLI, filesystem/network containment or remote provider cessation.
Use an existing approved runtime environment and exact profile for a separate
actual start/cancel/resume/tool/isolation campaign. No runtime installation,
credential change, model pull or provider fallback is implied.

The single-step 2.2 admission path currently admits only an explicitly trusted
`codex-v1-fixture/1` registration. The shared executor contract suite observes one
supervised fake CLI, real local cancellation, canonical/wire identity mapping and
independent synthetic verification. It also checks production/native-resume
refusal. The simulated provider declaration does not prove the actual endpoint,
account, model, instructions, tools or containment of any vendor CLI. Revocation
before dispatch or before owned gate release prevents target execution; retained
unknown windows remain quarantined rather than manufacturing cessation evidence.
Adding another shared driver case or installing a binary grants no runtime
authority. Production stays disabled until separately reviewed exact-mode proof.

Claude wire tests are original synthetic frames, not installed-version
transcripts. Its decoder is unregistered and reports untrusted protocol data;
no provider identity, billing proof, native-resume or cessation receipt follows.

The intended CI matrix is standard GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04 x64 and macOS 15
arm64, Python 3.11–3.14. A configured workflow is not evidence that those cells
passed; each requires its own exact-head results. Repository visibility does not
override runtime preflight or qualify an execution mode.

The explicit distribution inventory excludes control stores, credentials, user
homes, raw logs, Git history and unrelated source. Pattern screening is a
secondary check, not proof of arbitrary-secret absence or rights ownership.
Source-archive normalization removes tar ownership, extended metadata and build
timestamps without changing file payloads or modes. The auditor rejects those
headers if they return, optional wheel metadata, and unapproved package contact
or source-URL metadata. These checks complement the source/content review.
The project uses the [MIT License](../LICENSE). The auditor requires exactly
the approved MIT metadata and license bytes in source, wheel and sdist, while
rejecting additional identity/contact/source metadata. License and notice changes
require rebuilding and fresh qualification. Public visibility and registry
publication remain separate owner decisions.

## Claude fixture qualification scope

M5 implements the synthetic `claude-print-fixture/1` contract through the existing
owned supervisor/runner. The same public durable-driver tests cover Codex and

No real Claude start/cancel/resume, auth/routing, protective context/tool policy

environment observations, not actual HTTP or managed-settings isolation proof.

Shared contract cases cover worker/result separation, independent acceptance,
owned and closed-gate cancellation, persistent restart budgets and native refusal
for both profiles. Route/evidence negatives cover forwarding, unknown identity,
availability, auth, endpoint, mode, provenance, revocation and expiry. Format-5
maintenance must preserve complete prior state and exclude the byte-pinned M5
client. Source and installed artifact results qualify only their recorded head,
platform and synthetic mode; they do not enable production or real credentials.
External-server cessation and real token/cost accounting remain unsupported.
